widgets_values_named.title: Half a Job
widgets_values_named.style: trbdr, English, warm male vocal, modern alternative country and Americana, mid-tempo, dry intimate vocal, acoustic guitar, restrained overdriven electric guitar, melodic bass, loose natural drums, subtle organ, understated live-band feel, slightly rough around the edges, conversational and unforced, reflective without sentimentality, strong melodic chorus, organic contemporary production

widgets_values:
[Verse 1]
There's a bag of screws beside the sink
Been sitting there since early May
The cupboard door still drops an inch
But only if you pull it that way

You said you'd sort it when you had time
I said the same about the hall
We got good at living round things
That didn't really work at all

[Chorus]
Leave half a job for another day
Leave your coat where it shouldn't be
There's plenty here that could be better
Nothing here that needs to leave

Give me something slightly unfinished
And another year with you

[Verse 2]
We bought the paint but missed the wall
Changed our minds somewhere outside
Spent the money on a weekend
Came back Sunday satisfied

The garden leans towards the pavement
The spare key sticks when it gets cold
Every plan became a maybe
Somehow that's the one that held

[Bridge]
Maybe we'll get round to all of it
Maybe that's beside the point
There's a difference between giving up
And knowing what you can enjoy

[Final Chorus]
Leave half a job for another day
Let the cupboard hang that way
There's plenty here that could be better
We can leave it there today

Give me something slightly unfinished
And another year with you
